newsitem.title: GHANA: KLM expands Ghana flights to Ivory Coast.
newsitem.headline: KLM expands Ghana flights to Ivory Coast.

text.p: Dutch airline KLM will start twice-weekly flights between Amsterdam and Abidjan, Ivory Coast, on April 1, its West Africa manager said on Monday.
"Abidjan is to become our hub for French-speaking West Africa, like Accra is our hub for the Anglophone countries in the region," Bart van Es told Reuters.
At the same time KLM would stop its service to Conakry, Guinea, he added.
"Ivory Coast provides us with numerous facilities in the framework of its promotion of trade and tourism," said Van Es.

Abidjan, the hub for multinational airline Air Afrique and an important destination for Air France, is trying to woo more international carriers in line with the country's ambition of becoming a regional economic power.
Expansion and modernisatiom of the airport is one of Ivory Coast's 12 major construction projects intended to change the face of the country by the year 2000.
South Africa Airways launched a direct link between Johannesburg and Abidjan last month and Belgium's Sabena is expected to follow later in the first half of the year.
Using Boeing 767 aircraft, Amsterdam-Abidjan flights will stop in Freetown, Sierra Leone, with non-stop returns.
Apart from Ghana and Ivory Coast, KLM has four weekly return flights to Lagos, Nigeria, two to Kano in northern Nigeria and two to Lome, Togo.
It operates four weekly flights between Amsterdam and Accra. The fourth was inaugurated last month. A fifth flight is planned for later in the first quarter of 1997, Van Es said.
"Thanks to Ghana's political stability and economic development we are now planning to fly daily between Amsterdam and Accra by 1999," Van Es added.
